start.speaker: mirela
start.text: Mirela sets her stylus down and looks at you properly for the first time, the way a jeweller looks at a stone. 'You're the one carrying pieces of the Ember Crown. I've traced you across the kingdom on that orrery, and every time you picked up another piece, the figures moved.' She folds her gloved hands. 'So. You've climbed four hundred stairs to see the court mage. Either you're very stupid or you want something. Which?'

choices.text: Take out the shards and set them on her table.
'You move the frost on that orrery forward every morning. You know exactly how long Highspire has.'
[Persuasion] 'Help me take the heart-stone, and you're the mage who saved Vael. Not the one who kept the Regent's lamps lit.'
'Caul is gone and the figures are still bad. Come and check mine.'
'Another time.'

shards.speaker: mirela
shards.text: She doesn't touch them. She takes off one glove, very slowly, and holds her bare hand over them, and you watch the shards lean toward her warmth like seedlings to a window. 'They're alive,' she says, barely aloud. 'He told me the stone was dying and the shards would be dead glass. He told me—' She stops. Puts the glove back on. 'I've been doing the wrong sum. For four years.' She stands. 'I'm coming with you. I can get you into the Masque as my guest, and I can get you down his stair.'

conscience.speaker: mirela
conscience.text: For a moment the frost goes out of her entirely and she is just a tired woman at a cold machine. 'Eleven months,' she says. 'I check it every morning. Then I take my figures to Caul and he thanks me and the Tiers stay warm and the Stair freezes, and I go back up my tower.' She looks at you. 'Nobody has ever asked me about the orrery. They ask me what it says. Not what I think of it.' She gets her coat. 'I'll get you into the Masque. After that, we'll see.'

ambition.speaker: mirela
ambition.text: Mirela laughs, short and sharp. 'Flattery. Crude, obvious, and correct.' She taps the stylus against her teeth. 'The mage who saved Vael. It does have a better sound to it.' She stands. 'Very well. I'll bring you to the Masque as my guest, and you will try not to embarrass me in front of the Collegium.'

after.speaker: mirela
after.text: Mirela looks at the orrery for a long moment, at the red bead and the frost that nobody has moved forward this morning. 'Somebody ought to,' she says. 'You'll get them wrong otherwise.' She pulls her gloves on and takes her coat from the hook. 'I want it noted that I am coming because the arithmetic requires it, and for no other reason.'

cold.speaker: mirela
cold.text: 'No.' She picks the stylus up again. 'People have been trying to talk me into things since I was twelve. You'll have to do better than that. Come back when you have something I can't calculate.' But she doesn't send you away, either.

start.speaker: mirela
start.text: At the end of the silent hall, the tall glass figure turns its head, and the lantern in its chest brightens. Mirela stops dead. 'I designed it,' she says. 'Caul asked for a warden that would never sleep, never be bribed and never be sorry, and I gave him one in three weeks, and I was so proud of the lantern.' Her voice is perfectly steady. 'It will not let us pass. It knows me, and that makes no difference. I built it that way.'

choices.text: [Arcana] 'Then you know where you hid the flaw. Show me, and I'll hold it while you pull.'
Draw steel.
Back away down the hall.

wakes.text: The Glass Warden takes one step, and the sound it makes is the first sound in the Quiet Cells: a high, ringing, singing note like a wet finger round a goblet. It raises arms of glass edged like knives.

unmade.speaker: mirela
unmade.text: She talks you through it in a whisper: a line of script under the lantern, a seam in the glass, a word to hold and a word to say. You hold. She says. The Glass Warden stops mid-step and the lantern in its chest goes out, and it stands there clear and empty as a window. Mirela puts her hand flat on its chest. 'I always put a back door in,' she says. 'Even then. I never told him.'

start.text: In the last cell, a thin old man in the rags of a magister's robe is sitting very straight on a stone bench, doing sums in the frost on the wall with one finger. When the glass door swings open, he looks up, and his face lights. 'Mirela.' In the cell beside his, a big man with a beard to his chest gets slowly to his feet: Tobin Quill, who stood on a barrel and asked why the Stair was cold. Mirela stands in the doorway and doesn't move. 'Magister,' she says, and then nothing else at all.

choices.text: Touch her arm. 'Tell him. He should hear it from you.'
[Insight] Watch Fell's face. Ask him gently whether he already knows.
Say nothing. It is hers to tell, or not.

confess.speaker: mirela
confess.text: 'It was me,' Mirela says. 'I told Caul what you said in the Collegium. I knew what would happen. I wanted the post more than I wanted to be brave.' She is very pale. 'I'm sorry. That is not a sufficient sum, but it's the one I have.' Fell gets up, slowly, and crosses the cell, and takes both her gloved hands in his. 'I know, child. I knew the morning they came. You were frightened, and so was I, once.' He squeezes. 'You came. That's the figure that matters.'

knew.speaker: highspire_fell
knew.text: 'Of course I know.' Fell's voice is dry and kind. 'Who else heard me that day? Mirela, my dear, I taught you to check your figures. Did you think I wouldn't check mine?' Mirela makes a sound like ice cracking. He holds out his arms, and after a long moment, the court mage of Vael walks into them, gloves and all, and stays there.

silent.speaker: mirela
silent.text: Mirela says only, 'We're getting you out, Magister,' and gives him her coat, and does not look at him while she does it. Fell watches her with an odd, patient expression, as if he were waiting for a sum to come out. On the way back down the hall she walks very fast and does not speak to anyone. Later, when you look back, she is wiping her eyes with the back of a glove.

start.speaker: mirela
start.text: Mirela is sitting as close to the fire as she can without being in it, notebook on her knees, writing in figures so small they look like stitching. Her fingers, in their fingerless gloves, are blue at the tips. She does not look up. 'Three hundred and twenty,' she says. 'Days. Until the frost reaches the Ember Palace, if nothing changes. I work it out every night. Don't make a face. It's restful. If I know the number, it can't surprise me.'

choices.text: Take her hands between yours and hold them until they warm.
[Insight] 'It isn't restful. You count because you're frightened, and you've never told anyone.'
'Then I'll leave you to your sums. Goodnight, Mirela.' Leave her be.

hands.speaker: mirela
hands.text: She goes absolutely rigid, the way a cat does when picked up, and you think she is going to pull away. She doesn't. After a while, quietly: 'You're very warm. It's inefficient. You must waste a great deal of heat.' Her thumb moves, once, across your knuckles. 'I'm going to stop counting for tonight,' she says, as if confessing to a crime. 'Don't tell anyone.'

afraid.speaker: mirela
afraid.text: The stylus stops. For a long time she doesn't say anything. 'Since I was twelve,' she says finally, 'I have been the cleverest person in every room. Do you know what that means? It means nobody else is coming. If I get the sum wrong, there is no one to check it.' She looks at you, grey eyes very bright. 'You're checking it. I don't know what to do about that.'

choices.text: 'Let me check it with you. Every night, if you like.' Take her hand.
'You don't have to do anything about it. Just let someone else carry a figure or two.'

checked.speaker: mirela
checked.text: She looks down at your joined hands as if they were a proof she had not expected to work. 'Every night,' she repeats. 'That's a great many nights. You'd have to be very patient.' A pause. 'I'd make it worth your while. I'm extremely good at sums.' And then, astonishingly, she laughs, and puts her head on your shoulder, and stays there.

carry.speaker: mirela
carry.text: 'Three hundred and twenty,' she says, and hands you the notebook. 'You hold it, then. Just for tonight.' She closes her eyes, and is asleep before you can answer, the first time you have ever seen her sleep before you.

brush.speaker: mirela
brush.text: 'Don't analyse me,' she says, not unkindly. 'I'm the one who does that.' She bends back over the notebook. 'Go to sleep. I'll take first watch. I always do.'

declined.speaker: mirela
declined.text: 'Goodnight.' She sounds, for a moment, almost disappointed, and then the stylus starts scratching again. 'You're a better companion than most magisters,' she says to the notebook. 'That's not saying much. But it's saying something.'

start.speaker: mirela
start.text: Mirela hands you her notebook open at a page she has clearly torn out and put back three times. It is full of her tiny figures, all about the Thornwake: the cold, the shards, the days. In the middle of it all is a single letter, circled, with a great many arrows pointing at it and nothing at all pointing out. 'That's you,' she says. 'I can solve for everything else. I've been trying to solve for you since the Glass Tower, and every time I think I have, you do something unreasonable.' She folds her arms. 'Fell says I should tell you. Fell is an interfering old man.'

choices.text: Close the notebook gently, and kiss her.
'Then let's leave it unsolved, and find out together.'
'Some terms are better left as they are, Mirela. As friends.'

kiss.speaker: mirela
kiss.text: She makes a small surprised noise against your mouth and then kisses you back with exactly the same focus she gives the orrery, which is to say entirely. When she pulls away, her glasses, if she wore any, would be crooked. 'That,' she says, 'was empirical. I'll need to repeat it for the results to be valid.' She does.

together.speaker: mirela
together.text: Mirela looks at the circled letter for a long moment. Then she takes her stylus and, very carefully, draws a second circle overlapping the first, and writes her own initial in it. 'There,' she says, a little hoarse. 'A system of two. Much harder to solve. Much more interesting.' She does not give you the notebook back.

declined.speaker: mirela
declined.text: 'Friends.' She takes the notebook back, tears out the page, folds it small and puts it in her glove. 'Good. Yes. That's a clean solution.' She smiles, and it nearly reaches her eyes. 'I have very few friends. I'll try not to be a bad one.'

start.speaker: mirela
start.text: Mirela has put the notebook away. You have never seen her without it at night. She is sitting by the fire with her gloves off and her bare hands held out to it, and they are not blue. 'I stopped counting,' she says. 'Last week. I noticed this morning. I don't know the number any more.' She turns her head. 'I've run every sum I know about what happens after the Thornwake, and they all come out uncertain, except one. In every one of them I want you there at the end.' She swallows. 'That isn't a calculation. I'm aware of that.'

choices.text: Take her bare hands in yours. 'Then I'll be there.'

effects.message: Mirela takes a drop of Collegium glass on a silver chain from her pocket, a frost-flower caught inside it, and puts it round your neck with fingers that are, for once, perfectly warm. 'I made it the night I stopped counting,' she says. 'It's the only thing I've ever made that wasn't for anyone else.'

choices.text: 'Ask me again when the Thornwake is behind us.'
'Mirela, I can't promise you that.' Step back, gently.

later.speaker: mirela
later.text: 'That's reasonable,' she says, and it clearly costs her. 'I'll hold the figure open. I'm good at that.' She puts her gloves back on, one finger at a time, and then holds your hand anyway, gloved, until the fire goes out.

declined.speaker: mirela
declined.text: Mirela nods once, very precisely, as if you had corrected a sum of hers and been right. 'Thank you for telling me plainly,' she says. 'Most people don't.' She pulls her gloves back on. Her hands are steady. In the morning she is exactly as she always was, and only you notice that she never takes them off again.
